artworks.title: Eteocles and Polynices
artworks.description: Neoclassical oil by Giovanni Silvagni staging the mutual slaughter of Oedipus' sons before the gates of Thebes: Eteocles and Polynices lock shields and spears in the duel that ends the Seven's war and opens Antigone's tragedy. The brothers' interlocking bodies make the fratricide a single fatal knot — the image that later painters and urn-makers return to whenever they need the Theban civil war in one frame.

artworks.title: Eteocles and Polynices
artworks.description: Flemish cabinet picture in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (inv. 155): Francken crowds the Theban duel with spectators, armour, and the chaos of the Seven Against Thebes, keeping Eteocles and Polynices as the bright centre of the slaughter. The small panel translates Aeschylus' and Statius' civil war into Antwerp's taste for densely peopled mythological histories.

artworks.title: Duel of Eteocles and Polynices (Etruscan cinerary urn)
artworks.description: Alabaster cinerary urn relief in Siena's Museo Archeologico Nazionale: the Theban brothers thrust at each other while winged demons frame the fight — an Etruscan reading of the Greek fratricide used as a funerary emblem. Carved in the Hellenistic centuries, it shows how far west the duel of Eteocles and Polynices travelled as an image of civil strife and shared death.

artworks.title: The Seven Chiefs against Thebes
artworks.description: History painting exhibited at the Salon of 1827: Mongez gathers the Argive champions before the walls of Thebes, the army that Polynices leads against his brother's throne. Eteocles' city is the fortress under siege; the canvas turns Aeschylus' Seven into a grand Napoleonic-era battle machine, with the disputed kingship of Eteocles as the war's cause.

artworks.title: Eteocles and Polynices (detail)
artworks.description: Detail from Tiepolo's treatment of the Theban brothers: armour, gesture, and the locked struggle that leaves both kings dead on the same field. The Venetian painter keeps the duel as a flash of Baroque motion — Eteocles still the brother who held the city, Polynices the exile who came back with the Seven.

films.title: Antigone
films.description: Javellas' Antigone opens on the aftermath of Eteocles' war: the brother who held Thebes, buried with honour, while Polynices is left for the dogs — the decree that starts the tragedy.

music.title: Antigone
music.description: Honegger's opera inherits the brothers' mutual slaughter as given: Eteocles the buried king, the other side of the gate Creon will not name.

popCulture.title: La Thébaïde
popCulture.creator: Jean Racine
popCulture.description: Racine's first tragedy is the Theban brothers' civil war: Eteocles and Polynices destroying each other and their house before Antigone's story can begin.
